description: Serve repeated queries from a TTL-based cache and enforce a token-bucket budget governor per time window on the live-web path, returning a graceful "rate-limited, try later" response rather than hammering SearXNG or external engines.

requirements.description: Cache live-web search results using a TTL-based cache keyed on normalized query string, returning cached results for repeated queries without issuing SearXNG requests. Enforce a token-bucket budget governor on the live-web path: each external request consumes one token, tokens refill at a configured rate per time window, and when the bucket is exhausted the system returns a structured 'rate-limited, try later' response (HTTP 429 with retry-after hint) rather than forwarding the request to SearXNG. Cache and budget state must be inspectable via the ops panel.
requirements.title: Live-Web Result Cache with TTL and Token-Bucket Budget Governor

validation.notes: Cache key generation produces identical keys for semantically equivalent queries (same terms, different whitespace/case normalization)
Cache returns a hit for a query issued within TTL window after initial population
Cache returns a miss for a query issued after TTL expiry, triggering a fresh SearXNG request
Token bucket correctly refills to capacity after one full time window elapses
Token bucket returns exhausted=true and zero remaining tokens after burst limit is consumed
When bucket is exhausted, the live-web path returns a structured rate-limited response with retry-after field, not a SearXNG call
Token bucket refill is monotonic and does not exceed configured capacity
Issue the same query twice within TTL; assert SearXNG HTTP call count equals exactly one (second served from cache)
Exhaust the token bucket by issuing N+1 requests in one window; assert the N+1th returns a graceful rate-limited response and no additional SearXNG call is made

Default federated query issues zero external HTTP calls even when budget is exhausted (learnings path unaffected) [covering test lives in search-hub — the default auto path withholds SCOPE_EXTERNAL providers entirely, so web-search.live is never called regardless of budget state]
Cache hit response time must be under 50ms at p95 (no network I/O)
Budget governor check adds at most 1ms overhead to the request path
Repeated identical user queries are served from cache, reducing SearXNG load and preserving rate-limit budget
Users receive a clear 'rate-limited, try later' message rather than an error or silent failure when the budget is exhausted

title: Live-Web Result Cache and Budget Governor
